mainEntity.name: How much does a workers' comp lawyer cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Workers' comp lawyers typically work on a contingency fee basis. This means they only get paid if you win your case, either through a settlement or an award. Their fee is a percentage of the total benefits you receive, which is usually set by state law and approved by a workers' compensation judge. You generally won't pay upfront fees or hourly charges. This arrangement allows injured workers to access legal representation without financial burden during a difficult time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Workers' comp lawyers usually work on a contingency fee basis, meaning they are paid a percentage of your benefits only if you win your case. There are typically no upfront costs.
